newsitem.title: USA: Ford looking into China car market.
newsitem.headline: Ford looking into China car market.

text.p: Ford Motor Co, which plans to launch a line of light commercial vehicles in China this fall, is also exploring ways to enter the Chinese passenger car market, Vice Chairman Wayne Booker told reporters Thursday.
"We're doing various other studies to participate in the passenger car market," said Booker, who oversees the automaker's international operations.
The U.S. No. 2 automaker this fall plans to launch the Transit series with its Jiangling Motors Corp joint partner. Ford also has five component joint ventures in China.
Booker met with reporters at Ford's Dearborn, Mich., headquarters for an update on the company's one-third ownership of Mazda Motor Corp.

General Motors Corp is the only one of Detroit's Big Three to have a passenger car production agreement in China. Last month it signed an agreement to produce mid-sized sedans in a $1.57 billion joint venture with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp. Ford had also bid for the car contract GM received.
